subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should OpenClaw accept this coordinated breaking reshape of the unshipped and beta gateway-protocol families before publishing the package surface?
rationale: Whether the cited no-shipped-caller audit is sufficient to permit intentional beta protocol breakage is a release and public-API boundary decision that code review cannot infer safely.

options.title: Approve the pre-publication break
options.body: Accept the audited beta-only breakage after final CI and real behavior proof establish that all supported in-tree consumers use the new shapes.

options.title: Preserve beta compatibility temporarily
options.body: Keep the old protocol fields until a documented migration window or release boundary is selected, at the cost of retaining more surface.

options.title: Split the release-vintage work
options.body: Land only the additive vintage metadata and guard separately, then decide the contract reshapes in a narrower compatibility review.

recommendation.title: Approve the pre-publication break
recommendation.body: Accept the audited beta-only breakage after final CI and real behavior proof establish that all supported in-tree consumers use the new shapes.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the protocol audit and all supplied branch commits, making them the closest available routing candidate; final API acceptance remains a human repository decision.
